Its core innovation lies in combining tree-sitter parsing with local embeddings to form a hybrid search engine. The token reduction (~99%) arises from structured query optimization rather than raw data compression. This implies a dual regime: high-fidelity semantic retrieval and low-latency access. Failure modes include scalability degradation under large-scale changes and dependency on accurate grammar definitions. The derived kernel 'structural_query_token_reduction' models this efficiency gain mathematically, while 'incremental_graph_update' captures the dynamic evolution of the graph.
